statement: A straight line commensurable with a major straight line is itself also major.
heath_proof: Let AB be major, and let CD be commensurable with AB; I say that CD is major. Let AB be divided at E; therefore AE, EB are straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them rational, but the rectangle contained by them medial. [X. 39] Let the same construction be made as before. Then since, as AB is to CD, so is AE to CF, and EB to FD, therefore also, as AE is to CF, so is EB to FD. [V. 11] But AB is commensurable with CD; therefore AE, EB are also commensurable with CF, FD respectively. [X. 11] And since, as AE is to CF, so is EB to FD, alternately also, as AE is to EB, so is CF to FD; [V. 16] therefore also, componendo, as AB is to BE, so is CD to DF; [V. 18] therefore also, as the square on AB is to the square on BE, so is the square on CD to the square on DF. [VI. 20] Similarly we can prove that, as the square on AB is to the square on AE, so also is the square on CD to the square on CF. Therefore also, as the square on AB is to the squares on AE, EB, so is the square on CD to the squares on CF, FD; therefore also, alternately, as the square on AB is to the square on CD, so are the squares on AE, EB to the squares on CF, FD. [V. 16] But the square on AB is commensurable with the square on CD; therefore the squares on AE, EB are also commensurable with the squares on CF, FD. And the squares on AE, EB together are rational; therefore the squares on CF, FD together are rational. Similarly also twice the rectangle AE, EB is commensurable with twice the rectangle CF, FD. And twice the rectangle AE, EB is medial; therefore twice the rectangle CF, FD is also medial. [X. 23] Therefore CF, FD are straight lines incommensurable in square which make, at the same time, the sum of the squares on them rational, but the rectangle contained by them medial; therefore the whole CD is the irrational straight line called major. [X. 39] Therefore a straight line commensurable with the major straight line is major.
ai_proof_text:
10.68
**Statement:** A straight line commensurable with a major straight line is itself also major.

**Step 1.** Let A be a major straight line, and let B be commensurable in length with A. By 10.9, the squares A² and B² have the ratio of a square number to a square number. Therefore A² and B² are commensurable areas, by 10.6.

**Step 2.** Let r be the assigned rational straight line (D10.1.3). Construct fourth proportionals x and y such that r:A = A:x and r:B = B:y (6.12). Consequently, the rectangle contained by r and x equals A², and the rectangle contained by r and y equals B² (6.17).

**Step 3.** Since A is major, its square applied to the rational straight line r produces a fourth binomial as breadth (10.63). Thus x is a fourth binomial relative to r. Path choice: applying the square immediately reaches this fourth-binomial characterization, so we transfer its order rather than reconstruct the major's defining terms.

**Step 4.** Rectangles with the same altitude are to one another as their bases (6.1). Hence, using the equalities in Step 2, A²:B² = x:y. Since A² and B² are commensurable by Step 1, x and y are commensurable in length (10.11).

**Step 5.** A straight line commensurable in length with a binomial is itself binomial and of the same order (10.66). Since x is a fourth binomial, y is therefore also a fourth binomial relative to r.

**Step 6.** The side of an area contained by a rational straight line and a fourth binomial is major (10.57). Apply this to the rectangle contained by r and y. By Step 2 this rectangle equals B², so B is its square-side and is therefore major. Thus a straight line commensurable with a major straight line is itself also major.
